## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(gt)
library(scales)

DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp03")
fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE)

# Latest releases: ACS-1 for 2025, ACS-5 for 2020-2024.
ACS1_YEAR <- 2025
ACS5_YEAR <- 2024

# B01003_001 = total population. B02018_022 = Bangladeshi, alone or in any
# combination (checked against the Census variable list).
ACS_VARIABLES <- c(total_pop = "B01003_001", bangladeshi = "B02018_022")

NYC_COUNTIES <- c("Bronx", "Kings", "New York", "Queens", "Richmond")
```

## Data Acquisition

### Task 1: CBSA Population

```{r}
#| label: load-cbsa

load_cbsa_population <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, str_c("cbsa_acs5_", ACS5_YEAR, ".csv"))

  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    get_acs(
      geography = "cbsa",
      variables = ACS_VARIABLES,
      year = ACS5_YEAR,
      survey = "acs5"
    ) |>
      select(-moe) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
      write_csv(cache_file)
  }

  read_csv(cache_file, col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character()))
}

CBSA_POP <- load_cbsa_population()


load_us_total <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, str_c("us_acs5_", ACS5_YEAR, ".csv"))

  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    get_acs(
      geography = "us",
      variables = ACS_VARIABLES,
      year = ACS5_YEAR,
      survey = "acs5"
    ) |>
      select(-moe) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
      write_csv(cache_file)
  }

  read_csv(cache_file)
}

US_TOTAL <- load_us_total()
```

### Task 2: NYC Tract Population

```{r}
#| label: load-tracts
load_nyc_tracts <- function() {
  
  cache_file <- fs::path(
    DATA_DIR, str_c("nyc_tracts_acs5_", ACS5_YEAR, ".gpkg")
  )

  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    get_acs(
      geography = "tract",
      variables = ACS_VARIABLES,
      state = "NY",
      county = NYC_COUNTIES,
      year = ACS5_YEAR,
      survey = "acs5",
      geometry = TRUE
    ) |>
      select(-moe) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
      write_sf(cache_file)
  }

  read_sf(cache_file)
}

NYC_TRACTS <- load_nyc_tracts()
```

### Task 3: NYC Neighborhood Areas (NTAs)

```{r}
#| label: load-nta
load_nyc_nta <- function() {
  zip_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "nyc_nta2020.zip")
  unzip_dir <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "nta_shapefile")

 
  if (!fs::file_exists(zip_file)) {
    nta_url <- paste0(
      "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/api/geospatial/",
      "9nt8-h7nd?method=export&format=Shapefile"
    )
    download.file(nta_url, zip_file, mode = "wb")
  }

 
  unzip(zip_file, exdir = unzip_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  shp_path <- fs::dir_ls(unzip_dir, recurse = TRUE, glob = "*.shp")[1]

  st_read(shp_path, quiet = TRUE)
}

NYC_NTA <- load_nyc_nta()
```

### Task 4: Aggregate Tracts to NTAs

```{r}
#| label: aggregate-nta
NYC_TRACTS <- st_transform(NYC_TRACTS, st_crs(NYC_NTA))

TRACTS_IN_NTA <- NYC_TRACTS |>
  st_join(NYC_NTA, join = st_intersects, largest = TRUE)
NTA_POP <- TRACTS_IN_NTA |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(nta2020, ntaname, boroname) |>
  summarize(
    total_pop = sum(total_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    bangladeshi = sum(bangladeshi, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(bangladeshi_share = bangladeshi / total_pop)

NTA_MAP <- NYC_NTA |>
  left_join(NTA_POP, by = c("nta2020", "ntaname", "boroname"))
```


## Task 5: Download PLUTO


```{r}
#| label: load-pluto
library(httr2)

load_pluto <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "pluto.csv")
  keep_cols <- c(
    "borough", "bbl", "bct2020", "unitsres", "resarea",
    "officearea", "comarea", "bldgarea", "numfloors", "landuse"
  )

  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    base_url <- "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/64uk-42ks.csv"
    page_size <- 50000
    offset <- 0
    pages <- list()

    repeat {
      message("Downloading PLUTO rows from ", offset)
      page_text <- request(base_url) |>
        req_url_query(
          `$select` = paste(keep_cols, collapse = ","),
          `$order` = "bbl",          # stable order so paging doesn't skip rows
          `$limit` = page_size,
          `$offset` = offset
        ) |>
        req_timeout(180) |>
        req_retry(max_tries = 6, backoff = ~ min(60, 2 ^ .x)) |>
        req_perform() |>
        resp_body_string()

      page <- read_csv(I(page_text), show_col_types = FALSE)

      pages <- append(pages, list(page))
      
      if (nrow(page) < page_size) break
      offset <- offset + page_size
    }

    bind_rows(pages) |> write_csv(cache_file)
  }

  read_csv(
    cache_file,
    col_types = cols(
      bbl = col_character(),
      bct2020 = col_character(),
      borough = col_character(),
      .default = col_double()
    )
  )
}

PLUTO <- load_pluto()
```

## Task 6: Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
#| label: pluto-tract

BORO_FIPS <- c(MN = "061", BX = "005", BK = "047", QN = "081", SI = "085")

PLUTO_TRACT <- PLUTO |>
  filter(!is.na(bct2020), borough %in% names(BORO_FIPS)) |>
  mutate(
    tract6 = str_pad(str_sub(bct2020, 2), width = 6, side = "left", pad = "0"),
    GEOID  = str_c("36", BORO_FIPS[borough], tract6)
  ) |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarize(
    officearea = sum(officearea, na.rm = TRUE),
    comarea    = sum(comarea,    na.rm = TRUE),
    resarea    = sum(resarea,    na.rm = TRUE),
    bldgarea   = sum(bldgarea,   na.rm = TRUE),
    unitsres   = sum(unitsres,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


TRACT_NTA <- TRACTS_IN_NTA |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(GEOID, nta2020, ntaname, boroname)

matched <- sum(PLUTO_TRACT$GEOID %in% NYC_TRACTS$GEOID)
cat("PLUTO tracts:", nrow(PLUTO_TRACT),
    "| matched to census tracts:", matched,
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)", 100 * matched / nrow(PLUTO_TRACT)), "\n")

```

```{r}
#| label: tract-stats
TRACT_STATS <- NYC_TRACTS |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, total_pop, bangladeshi) |>
  left_join(PLUTO_TRACT, by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(TRACT_NTA |> select(GEOID, ntaname, boroname), by = "GEOID")
```

### Q1 Which NYC census tract has the most office floor area in NYC?

```{r}
#| label: q1-office
office_top <- TRACT_STATS |> slice_max(officearea, n = 1)

TRACT_STATS |>
  arrange(desc(officearea)) |>
  select(GEOID, ntaname, boroname, officearea) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)
```
### Q3. Which NYC census tract has the highest population density, measured as population per square foot of residential space? Do your answers change if you measure by population per residential unit?

```{r}
#| label: q3-density

TRACT_DENSITY <- TRACT_STATS |>
  filter(total_pop >= 500, unitsres >= 100, resarea >= 50000) |>
  mutate(
    pop_per_1k_sqft = total_pop / resarea * 1000,
    pop_per_unit    = total_pop / unitsres
  )

TRACT_DENSITY |>
  arrange(desc(pop_per_1k_sqft)) |>
  select(GEOID, ntaname, total_pop, resarea, pop_per_1k_sqft) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

# Ranked by residential unit
TRACT_DENSITY |>
  arrange(desc(pop_per_unit)) |>
  select(GEOID, ntaname, total_pop, unitsres, pop_per_unit) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)
```

### Q5. At a not-too-granular level, describe the distribution of ancestries in a large non-NYC city of your choosing from the previous question.

```{r}
#| label: q5-ancestry-dist
FEATURE_METRO <- "Washington-Arlington-Alexandria"
feature_geoid <- CBSA_POP |> filter(str_detect(NAME, FEATURE_METRO)) |> pull(GEOID)

load_cbsa_ancestry <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, str_c("b02018_cbsa_", ACS5_YEAR, ".csv"))
  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    get_acs(geography = "cbsa", table = "B02018",
            year = ACS5_YEAR, survey = "acs5") |>
      write_csv(cache_file)
  }
  read_csv(cache_file, col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character()))
}

B02018_CBSA <- load_cbsa_ancestry()

b02018_labels <- load_variables(ACS5_YEAR, "acs5") |>
  filter(str_starts(name, "B02018"), name != "B02018_001") |>
  transmute(variable = name, ancestry = str_remove(label, "^.*!!")) |>
  filter(!str_detect(ancestry, ":$"))

METRO_ANCESTRY <- B02018_CBSA |>
  filter(GEOID == feature_geoid, variable != "B02018_001") |>
  left_join(b02018_labels, by = "variable") |>
  filter(!is.na(ancestry)) |>
  arrange(desc(estimate))

plot_anc <- bind_rows(
  METRO_ANCESTRY |> slice_head(n = 10),
  METRO_ANCESTRY |> filter(ancestry == "Bangladeshi")
) |> distinct()

plot_anc |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(ancestry, estimate),
             fill = ancestry == "Bangladeshi")) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#006a4e", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Asian ancestry in the Washington, D.C. metro area",
    x = "Population",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}

  select(GEOID, ntaname, total_pop) |>

load_nyc_education <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, str_c("nyc_edu_acs5_", ACS5_YEAR, ".csv"))
  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    edu_vars <- c(edu_total = "B15003_001", bach = "B15003_022",

            year = ACS5_YEAR, survey = "acs5") |>
      select(GEOID, variable, estimate) |>

      write_csv(cache_file)
  }
  read_csv(cache_file, col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character()))
}

NYC_EDU <- load_nyc_education()
```

```{r}
#| label: ec-edu-analysis
EDU_TRACTS <- NYC_EDU |>
  mutate(bach_plus = bach + mast + prof + doct) |>
  left_join(TRACT_NTA |> select(GEOID, ntaname), by = "GEOID")

NTA_EDU <- EDU_TRACTS |>
  filter(!is.na(ntaname)) |>
  group_by(ntaname) |>
  summarize(bach_plus = sum(bach_plus, na.rm = TRUE),
            edu_total = sum(edu_total, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct_bach_plus = bach_plus / edu_total)

city_bach_plus <- sum(EDU_TRACTS$bach_plus, na.rm = TRUE) /
                  sum(EDU_TRACTS$edu_total, na.rm = TRUE)

BD_EDU <- NTA_POP |>
  slice_max(bangladeshi, n = 10) |>
  left_join(NTA_EDU, by = "ntaname") |>
  select(ntaname, boroname, bangladeshi, pct_bach_plus)

BD_EDU |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(ntaname = "Neighborhood", boroname = "Borough",
             bangladeshi = "Bangladeshi residents",
             pct_bach_plus = "Bachelor's degree or higher") |>
  fmt_number(columns = bangladeshi, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = pct_bach_plus, decimals = 1)

```

### Task 7 Atlas Communities of Entry

As a Bangladeshi American, I was inspired to research and analyze the Bangladeshi population and learned a lot of new things myself!

The New York metro area is home to `r comma(ny_bd)` of the `r comma(us_bd)` Bangladeshis. That’s about `r percent(ny_share, 1)`, enough to make New York the clear capital of Bangladeshi America.

#### History

The first Bengali immigrants to the U.S included silk merchants in the late 1800s and sailors in the early 1900s, some of whom settled in Harlem. The Immigration Act of 1924 largely blocked immigration from Asia, but the Immigration Act of 1965 ended quotas based on national origin and made it easier for skilled workers and family members to immigrate. After Bangladesh gained independence in 1971, more Bangladeshis came to the U.S. to study, work, or join family. The Immigration Act of 1990 created the Diversity Visa lottery, which helped the community grow, especially in New York City.

Before Bangladesh was a country, Bengali silk merchants were already arriving at Ellis Island. Where did they put down roots?


#### Where New York’s Bangladeshi community lives

Jamaica ranks first in the city, with about about `r comma(jamaica_bd)` Bangladeshi residents, `r queens_top` of the ten with the largest Bangladeshi populations are in Queens. Jackson Heights is another hub, but follow the map across borough lines and you’ll find communities in Kensington, Brooklyn, and Parkchester, in the Bronx.

```{r}
#| label: atlas-bd-map
ggplot(NTA_MAP) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = bangladeshi), color = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#006a4e", high = "#f42a41",
                      labels = comma, trans = "sqrt") +
  labs(fill = "Bangladeshi residents") +
  theme_void()
```

Even within Queens, the neighborhoods can look quite different. The income figure for Jamaica is about `r dollar(round(jamaica_inc, -2))`  compared with $91,600 in nearby Jamaica Estates and `r dollar(round(city_income, -2))` city average. The share of residents with a bachelor’s degree or higher ranges from ranges from `r percent(bach_min, 0.1)` to `r percent(bach_max, 0.1)` in my analysis, compared with `r percent(city_bach_plus, 0.1)` city wide. 

#### Beyond New York


```{r}
#| label: atlas-us-map
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
# US metros sized/colored by Bangladeshi population (bubble map, lower 48).

load_cbsa_geo <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, str_c("cbsa_bd_geo_", ACS5_YEAR, ".gpkg"))
  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    get_acs(geography = "cbsa", variables = c(bangladeshi = "B02018_022"),
            year = ACS5_YEAR, survey = "acs5", geometry = TRUE) |>
      select(GEOID, NAME, bangladeshi = estimate) |>
      write_sf(cache_file)
  }
  read_sf(cache_file)
}

load_us_states <- function() {
  cache_file <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "us_states.gpkg")
  if (!fs::file_exists(cache_file)) {
    get_acs(geography = "state", variables = c(pop = "B01003_001"),
            year = ACS5_YEAR, survey = "acs5", geometry = TRUE) |>
      select(GEOID, NAME) |>
      write_sf(cache_file)
  }
  read_sf(cache_file)
}

CBSA_GEO  <- load_cbsa_geo()
US_STATES <- load_us_states()

# Contiguous 48 (+ DC); drop AK, HI, PR, and territories.
drop_fips <- c("02", "15", "60", "66", "69", "72", "78")
states_48 <- US_STATES |> filter(!substr(GEOID, 1, 2) %in% drop_fips)

# Metro centroids with a Bangladeshi population, cropped to the lower 48.
metro_pts <- CBSA_GEO |> filter(bangladeshi > 0) |> st_centroid()
mp_xy <- st_coordinates(metro_pts)
metro_pts <- metro_pts |>
  mutate(lon = mp_xy[, 1], lat = mp_xy[, 2]) |>
  filter(lon > -125, lon < -66, lat > 24, lat < 50)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = states_48, fill = "#eef3f1", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = metro_pts, aes(size = bangladeshi, color = bangladeshi),
          alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 14, labels = comma) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#006a4e", high = "#f42a41", guide = "none") +
  coord_sf(crs = 5070) +
  labs(size = "Bangladeshi residents") +   # TODO: your own title + caption
  theme_void()


```

On the U.S. bubble map, New York stands out, but the population is concentrated well beyond that one metro. The ten metros with the largest Bangladeshi populations together account for about about `r percent(sum(slice_max(CBSA_POP, bangladeshi, n = 10)$bangladeshi) / US_TOTAL$bangladeshi, 2)` of the national total. Look at local population shares instead of head counts, though, and Buffalo moves to the top outside New York, followed by Buffalo, Atlantic City, Detroit, Washington D.C., Bridgeport. Washington is an interesting contrast. It stands out in that comparison, yet Bangladeshis are only about the only about the `r scales::label_ordinal()(which(METRO_ANCESTRY$ancestry == "Bangladeshi"))`largest Asian group in the Washington metro area.

Back in New York one can explore Bangladeshi culture and life here in the Big Apple! Start with the Bangladeshi groceries on Hillside Avenue, stop for fuchka from a cart in Jackson Heights, or head up to Starling Avenue in the Bronx, where a stretch of storefronts became known as Bangla Bazaar.
